method: FEA weighted 2028 presidential primary averages from public feeds (VoteHub individual polls, CC BY 4.0; Wikipedia nationwide primary tables, CC BY-SA; plus Pollfinity when a primary track is published). Identical surveys are collapsed across sources before weighting. Soft exponential recency decay with no short hard cutoff. When recent polling is thick the half-life shortens (about 10–21 days); when it is thin the half-life lengthens (up to about 45 days) and the look-back window widens. Within each pollster, polls are recency-weighted; pollsters are then weighted by the recency of their latest poll, with a mild quality prior. LV beats RV beats adults when the same release reports multiple populations. Each candidate’s average uses only polls that explicitly tested them. Headline standings favor candidates tested in a large share of recent polls; others appear in an expanded list. Candidates need at least four tested polls in the window. Poll shares are not renormalized to 100. Undecided/Other omitted. This is FEA’s own aggregate, not VoteHub’s, Wikipedia’s, or Pollfinity’s published average.
